units.t: Place Value to One Million and Rounding

learn: Each place is ten times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions.
In 482,365 the 8 is in the ten thousands place, so it means 80,000.
Commas separate groups of three digits, called periods.
check: Each place is ___ times the place to its right.
lessons.try: Write 709,214 in expanded form.

learn: Read 305,040 as "three hundred five thousand, forty".
To compare, start at the greatest place value.
452,000 > 425,000 because 5 ten thousands > 2 ten thousands.
lessons.try: Order these from least to greatest: 98,765; 102,345; 99,999.

learn: Find the place you're rounding to and look at the digit to its right.
5 or more rounds up; less than 5 rounds down.
63,482 rounded to the nearest thousand is 63,000. Rounded to the nearest ten thousand it is 60,000.
check: 847,519 to the nearest hundred thousand is...
lessons.try: Round 847,519 to the nearest thousand and hundred thousand.

learn: Line up digits by place value and add from right to left.
Regroup when a column totals 10 or more.
check: When a column totals 10 or more, you...

learn: Subtract right to left, regrouping when the top digit is smaller.
Regrouping across zeros: 50,000 - 23,456 = 26,544.
Check by adding the difference to the number subtracted.
lessons.try: Subtract 80,302 - 47,568 and check.

learn: Round numbers to estimate before calculating.
If your exact answer is far from the estimate, recheck.
check: If an answer is far from the estimate, you...
lessons.try: Estimate, then solve: 612,450 - 298,700.

learn: Multiplying by 10 shifts each digit one place left: 45 × 10 = 450.
× 100 shifts two places: 45 × 100 = 4,500. × 1,000 shifts three: 45,000.
lessons.try: Solve 7 × 400 and 30 × 50.

learn: Or the standard algorithm, multiplying ones first and regrouping.
Estimate first: 4 × 300 = 1,200.
check: Partial products break a number by...
lessons.try: Multiply 6 × 1,457.

learn: The standard algorithm multiplies by the ones, then the tens (with a zero placeholder), then adds.
lessons.try: Draw an area model for 32 × 14.

learn: Sometimes a number can't be divided evenly. What's left over is the remainder.
17 ÷ 5 = 3 R2, because 5 × 3 = 15 and 2 are left.
The remainder is always less than the divisor.
lessons.try: Share 23 coins among 4 people. How many each, and how many left?

learn: Long division steps: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Repeat.
Check by multiplying: 213 × 4 = 852.
check: What is the step after subtract?
lessons.try: Divide 936 ÷ 3 and check.

learn: In word problems, decide what the remainder means.
30 students in vans of 8: 30 ÷ 8 = 3 R6, so you need 4 vans (round up).
30 cookies shared among 8: each gets 3, with 6 left (ignore or share the rest).
check: 30 students, vans hold 8. How many vans?
50 eggs in cartons of 12: full cartons?
50 eggs in cartons of 12: eggs left?
lessons.try: 50 eggs go in cartons of 12. How many full cartons? How many eggs left?

learn: Factors are numbers multiplied to make a product. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
Factor pairs: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4.
Every number has at least two factors: 1 and itself.
check: Every number has at least the factors 1 and...
lessons.try: List all factors of 24.

learn: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13 are prime.
A composite number has more than two factors: 4, 6, 8, 9.
1 is neither prime nor composite.
lessons.try: Find all prime numbers from 1 to 30.

learn: Multiples are the products of a number and counting numbers: multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24...
A pattern follows a rule: start at 3, add 4: 3, 7, 11, 15...
Look for features: all terms in "start 3, add 4" are odd.
check: Start at 3, add 4. What is the 5th term?
lessons.try: Make a pattern with the rule "start at 5, multiply by 2". Write 5 terms.

learn: Multiply or divide the numerator and denominator by the same number to make equivalent fractions.
2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12 (multiply by 2, then 2 again).
Simplifying: 6/8 = 3/4 (divide both by 2).
check: To make equivalent fractions, multiply top and bottom by...
lessons.try: Find three fractions equivalent to 3/5.

learn: Benchmark fractions like 0, 1/2 and 1 help compare.
3/8 is less than 1/2 (4/8). 5/6 is more than 1/2.
lessons.try: Compare 2/5 and 7/10 using 1/2 as a benchmark.

learn: To compare fractions with different denominators, rewrite them with a common denominator.
Compare 3/4 and 5/6: 3/4 = 9/12, 5/6 = 10/12. So 5/6 is greater.
Then compare the numerators.
lessons.try: Compare 2/3 and 3/5 using a common denominator.

learn: With the same denominator, add or subtract the numerators: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.
The denominator stays the same because the size of parts doesn't change.
check: When adding like fractions, the denominator...

learn: A mixed number has a whole number and a fraction: 2 1/4.
2 1/4 = 9/4 because 2 wholes = 8/4, plus 1/4.
Add mixed numbers by adding wholes and fractions: 1 2/5 + 2 1/5 = 3 3/5.
lessons.try: Write 3 2/3 as an improper fraction.

learn: Multiply the whole number by the numerator: 4 × 3/8 = 12/8 = 1 1/2.
The denominator stays the same.
lessons.try: A recipe needs 3/4 cup of flour per batch. How much for 3 batches?

learn: Decimals are another way to write fractions with denominators of 10 or 100.
3/10 = 0.3 (three tenths). 45/100 = 0.45 (forty-five hundredths).
The decimal point separates whole numbers from parts.
lessons.try: Write 7/10 and 62/100 as decimals.

learn: Compare decimals by place value, starting from the left.
0.6 > 0.45 because 6 tenths > 4 tenths.
Adding a zero doesn't change value: 0.6 = 0.60.
lessons.try: Order 0.7, 0.07 and 0.65 from least to greatest.

learn: Money uses decimals: $3.25 means 3 dollars and 25 hundredths of a dollar (25 cents).
3/10 of a dollar is 30 cents = $0.30.
3/10 = 30/100, so you can add tenths and hundredths by converting: 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.
lessons.try: Add 2/10 + 15/100 as a fraction and a decimal.

learn: 1 foot = 12 inches. 1 yard = 3 feet. 1 mile = 5,280 feet.
1 metre = 100 centimetres. 1 kilometre = 1,000 metres. 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams.
To convert a larger unit to a smaller one, multiply.
lessons.try: Convert 5 feet to inches and 3 kilometres to metres.

learn: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 1 minute = 60 seconds.
1 gallon = 4 quarts. 1 quart = 2 pints. 1 pint = 2 cups.
1 litre = 1,000 millilitres.
check: How many cups in a gallon?
lessons.try: How many cups are in a gallon?

learn: Area of a rectangle = length × width. Perimeter = 2 × (length + width).
A 9 m by 4 m garden has area 36 square metres and perimeter 26 metres.
If you know area and one side, divide to find the other side.
check: Area of a 9 m by 4 m rectangle is...
Perimeter of a 9 m by 4 m rectangle is...
Area 48 sq ft, width 6 ft. Length?
lessons.try: A rectangle has area 48 sq ft and width 6 ft. Find its length and perimeter.

learn: A line goes on forever in both directions. A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one endpoint.
Parallel lines never meet. Perpendicular lines meet at right angles.
Intersecting lines cross at a point.
lessons.try: Find parallel and perpendicular lines in your room.

learn: Angles are measured in degrees with a protractor.
A right angle is 90°. An acute angle is less than 90°. An obtuse angle is more than 90° but less than 180°.
A straight angle is 180°. A full turn is 360°.
lessons.try: Use a protractor (or app) to measure three angles in your home.

learn: Triangles can be classified by angles: right, acute or obtuse.
Quadrilaterals are classified by parallel sides and angles: a parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides.
A line of symmetry divides a shape into two matching halves. A square has 4 lines of symmetry.
check: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
A triangle with a 90° angle is a...
lessons.try: Fold paper shapes to find their lines of symmetry.
